進位開府 is promotion to the honor 開府 'opener of the government', not 'grand prefect'.
He had thirty thousand armored men. At the first news of Jinyang's fall he asked to march north; his memorials went unanswered, and Yongye burned with indignation.
He had thirty thousand armored men. At the first news of the defeat at Jinzhou he asked to march north; his memorial was shelved without reply, and Yongye burned with indignation.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang; 晉州敗 is the defeat at Jinzhou.
In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.
In the second year of Daxiang he was killed by campaign commander Cui Yanmu.
大象 is the Zhou era Daxiang, not 'Elephant'; 崔彥睦 is Cui Yanmu, not Yanmin.
In Elephant year 2 he was killed by campaigning general-in-chief Cui Yanmin.
In the second year of Daxiang he was killed by campaign area commander Cui Yanmu.
大象 is the era name Daxiang; 睦 is mu, not min.
His father Yuanying was grand master of splendid parallels and governor of northern Yu province.
His father Yuanying was equal in ceremony to the three excellencies and inspector of Northern Weizhou.
儀同 is 'equal in ceremony (to the Three Excellencies)'; 北蔚州 is Northern Weizhou, not 'northern Yu province'.
Fu took the army young and rose by battle merit to grand prefect and chief of the Yongqiao tribal settlement.
Fu joined the army young and by battle merit rose to opener of the government and grand commander of the people of Yongqiao.
開府 is the honor 'opener of the government', not 'grand prefect'; 領民大都督 commands the settled people, not a 'tribal settlement'.
The Zhou took Jinyang and captured circuit commissioner Wei Xianggui, whom they sent to summon Fu; Fu refused.
The Zhou took Jinzhou and captured branch commissioner Wei Xianggui, whom they sent to summon Fu; Fu refused.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽).
The Later Sovereign marched in person to relieve Jinyang and made Fu right vice minister of the circuit.
The Later Sovereign marched in person to relieve Jinzhou and made Fu right vice director of the branch department.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽).
The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with his son Shikuan to summon Fu: "Bingzhou is pacified. We send your son with the news—submit now."
The Zhou took Bingzhou and sent Wei Xiaokuan with Fu's son Shikuan to summon Fu: "Bingzhou is pacified, so we send your son to report it; you should submit at once."
其子世寬 is Fu Fu's son, as 公兒 'your son' confirms; 'his son' wrongly suggests Wei Xiaokuan's son.
The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinyang and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred men to the Fen to summon Fu.
The Zhou emperor returned from Ye to Jinzhou and sent Gao Anaigong and more than a hundred men to the Fen to summon Fu.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽).

He drew Fu aside to eat with him, lodged him with the attendant guard, made him grand master of splendid parallels, and charged him, "If I give you high rank at once, those who surrender will waver. Serve well—you will not lack wealth or honor."

He drew Fu aside to eat with him, lodged him with the attendant guard, made him supreme equal in ceremony, and charged him, "If I give you high rank at once, those who surrender will waver. Serve well—you will not lack wealth or honor."
上儀同 is 'supreme equal in ceremony', not 'grand master of splendid parallels'.
After the Qi defeat at Jinyang, few officers kept their honor intact.
After the Qi defeat at Jinzhou, few officers kept their honor intact.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽).

Among those who died to perfect loyalty was grand master of splendid parallels Chigan Gousheng, garrisoning southern Yan province. When the Zhou took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.
Among those who died to perfect loyalty was Chigan Gousheng, equal in ceremony, who garrisoned Southern Yanzhou. When the Zhou emperor took Ye and the amnesty arrived, Gousheng hanged himself.
儀同 is 'equal in ceremony'; 周帝破鄴 names the Zhou emperor.
There was also grand prefect and palace attendant eunuch Tian Jingxuan, originally named Peng, a barbarian.
There was also the eunuch Tian Jingxuan, opener of the government and inner palace attendant, originally styled Peng, a Man tribesman.
開府 is 'opener of the government', not 'grand prefect'; 本字鵬 means originally styled Peng; 蠻人 is a Man tribesman.
There was also Lei Xianhe, who after Jinyang's fall became left vice minister of the Jianzhou circuit.
There was also Lei Xianhe, who after the defeat at Jinzhou became left vice director of the Jianzhou circuit branch department.
晉州 is Jinzhou, not Jinyang (晉陽).
After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent grand prefect Hexi Yong'an to beg emergency aid of the Türk qaghan Tabo.
After the Later Sovereign lost Bingzhou he sent Hexi Yong'an, opener of the government, to beg emergency aid of the Türk Tabo Qaghan.
開府 is 'opener of the government', not 'grand prefect'.
Fu Fu's sons and men like them met an hour out of joint; before the gale came, who could tell which blade of grass would stand unbowed?
Master Fu and his like met an hour out of joint; before the gale came, who could tell which blade of grass would stand unbowed?
傅子 is the honorific 'Master Fu' (Fu Fu himself), not 'Fu Fu's sons'.
